products.description:
Close the Security-Options findings no other product owns

Every Windows fleet assessment leaves a short list of interactive-logon and network-access Security Options that the NTLM/SMB, RDP, and credential-theft products don't touch. This solution hardens exactly those four leftover findings through a single Intune Settings Catalog profile on enrolled Windows 10/11 devices — no Group Policy, no imaging, fully reversible — and complements a CIS/STIG baseline.

The four controls

  • Prohibit connection to non-domain networks while on a domain-authenticated network — stops a bridged path off the trusted LAN (fBlockNonDomain=1).
  • Smart card removal behavior = Lock Workstation — pulling the card locks the session (scremoveoption=1).
  • Disable automatic restart sign-on — the last user is not silently re-signed-in after an update reboot (DisableAutomaticRestartSignOn=1).
  • Do not display network selection UI — no network picker at the sign-in screen (DontDisplayNetworkSelectionUI=1).

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered Settings Catalog steps with full navigation paths; the one profile you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates and registry spot-checks.

Honest about user impact

Disabling automatic restart sign-on means users sign in again after an update reboot — the intended, more-secure behavior. The guide gives you the one-line notice to set that expectation before rollout.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — what each of the four controls does, the exact values, the honest user-impact, and how this pack is gap-only and complements NTLM/SMB, RDP, credential-theft, and CIS/STIG baselines.
  • Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Intune enrollment, Settings Catalog, existing-owner check, smart-card / network context, a pilot group) with how to verify/implement each.
  • Implementation Guide — exact steps to build the one named Settings Catalog profile with all four settings, assign it, deploy, and validate on a pilot.
  • 5 PowerShell scripts — readiness discovery, per-device applied-state validation, a coverage report, safe remediation that creates the profile, and a target-group builder.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (applied values, baseline conflicts, the “Disabled-means-on” inversion) plus Best Practices for owning each setting once.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

The leftover interactive-logon and network-access Security-Options findings closed across the Windows fleet — hardened and proven on a pilot before you scale.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • WINSECOPT-Discovery.ps1 — tenant readiness check for the four hardening settings
    • WINSECOPT-Validation.ps1 — validate assignment and per-device applied state
    • WINSECOPT-Report.ps1 — coverage report across Windows devices
    • WINSECOPT-Remediation.ps1 — safely create the Settings Catalog profile if missing
    • WINSECOPT-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — set the target group for the hardening profile

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
